title: Dwyer--Kan equivalences of homotopy Segal spaces preserve diagonal homotopy type
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, Kan complexes, weak homotopy equivalences and homotopy fibers as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. A simplicial space is a functor $X:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$; its diagonal has $(\operatorname{diag}X)_n=(X_n)_n$. Call $X$ a homotopy Segal space if each $X_n$ is Kan and, for every $n\geq2$, the consecutive-edge map
$$X_n\longrightarrow X_1\mathbin{\times^h_{X_0}}\cdots\mathbin{\times^h_{X_0}}X_1$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence. The product on the right has $n$ factors, with target of one edge matched to source of the next; each homotopy pullback of maps $a:U\to Z$ and $b:V\to Z$ of Kan complexes is modeled by $U\times_{Z,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,Z)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,Z}V$. The displayed consecutive-edge map uses the constant path at each common vertex. For vertices $x,y\in(X_0)_0$ put $M_X(x,y)=\operatorname{hofib}_{(x,y)}((d_1,d_0):X_1\to X_0\times X_0)$. The category $hX$ has these vertices as objects and $\pi_0M_X(x,y)$ as morphisms, with identity induced by $s_0$ and composition induced by the degree-two Segal comparison and $d_1:X_2\to X_1$; the simplicial identities give its associative unital composition. Let $F:X\to Y$ be a map of homotopy Segal spaces. Assume that $M_X(x,y)\to M_Y(Fx,Fy)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every pair $x,y$, and that every object of $hY$ is isomorphic to some $F(x)$. Then $\operatorname{diag}F:\operatorname{diag}X\to\operatorname{diag}Y$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Reedy fibrancy of $X,Y$ is not required.

source.place: Sections 4-5 (Segal spaces and homotopy categories), Theorem 7.7, and Section 12 (localizing at the spine inclusions and F(0) -> E). The stated levelwise Kan, homotopy-Segal and diagonal formulation is an agent-specified consequence using Reedy replacement and the fact that these localizing maps have weakly equivalent diagonals; it is not a verbatim theorem of the source. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-homotopy theorem.

proof.text: Choose functorial Reedy fibrant replacements $r_X:X\to RX$ and $r_Y:Y\to RY$ using [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] in the Kan model category of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Because $X_0,Y_0$ are already Kan, keep the degree-zero factorizations equal to the identity followed by the terminal fibration, as the prescribed-degree-zero clause permits. Thus $(RX)_0=X_0$, $(RY)_0=Y_0$, and $RF$ is a map with the same object function as $F$. Each $r_{X,n},r_{Y,n}$ is a weak equivalence. Naturality of the consecutive-edge maps and repeated application of [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] show that the homotopy Segal comparisons for $RX,RY$ are weak equivalences. At degree one Reedy fibrancy says that $(RX)_1\to X_0^2$ and $(RY)_1\to Y_0^2$ are Kan fibrations. Their strict mapping fibers therefore represent the homotopy fibers, by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]; their strict iterated edge products likewise compute the homotopy products. Hence $RX,RY$ are Segal spaces in Rezk's Reedy-fibrant convention. Homotopy-pullback invariance, applied to the endpoint maps and the fixed points $(x,y)$, identifies $M_X(x,y)\to M_{RX}(x,y)$ and the corresponding maps for $Y$ as weak equivalences. These maps preserve identities and composition: both compositions are obtained from the same natural diagram of the degree-two Segal comparison and $d_1$, and taking its inverse on homotopy classes commutes with these weak equivalences. Thus the two homotopy categories have unchanged objects and bijective Hom sets, and $RF$ has the mapping-space and essential-surjectivity hypotheses of $F$. Finally [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] makes $\operatorname{diag}r_X,\operatorname{diag}r_Y$ weak equivalences. It suffices, by the commuting square and two-out-of-three, to handle the Reedy-fibrant map $G=RF:U=RX\to V=RY$.

source.place: Sections 2.4 and 4.1; agent extension to levelwise Kan homotopy Segal spaces by Reedy replacement fixing degree zero.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-rezk-explicit-completion] to $U,V$. Write $H=\widehat G$ for the induced map; naturality gives $H i_U=i_VG$. The two completion units induce weak equivalences on mapping spaces. For any vertices $x,y$ of $U_0$, the mapping-space square and two-out-of-three from [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] therefore make
$$M_{\widehat U}(i_Ux,i_Uy)\longrightarrow M_{\widehat V}(H i_Ux,H i_Uy)$$
a weak equivalence. The completion theorem also makes $\widehat U,\widehat V$ Reedy-fibrant complete Segal spaces, so their mapping spaces may be taken to be strict endpoint fibers.

source.place: Section 14, natural completion and assertions (1),(3); mapping-space square at image objects.

proof.text:
We record the elementary naturality calculation needed below. For a map $f:A\to B$ of Reedy-fibrant Segal spaces and a fixed object triple, use [lem-coef-segal-composition-equivalences] to choose sections $s_A,s_B$ of the triangle comparisons $\theta_A,\theta_B$, and put $c_A=d_1s_A$, $c_B=d_1s_B$. That node states $d_1\simeq c_B\theta_B$. Precomposing this homotopy with the triangle map $f_2s_A$ gives
$$f_1c_A=d_1f_2s_A\simeq c_B\theta_B f_2s_A=c_B(f_1\times f_1),$$
since $\theta_B f_2=(f_1\times f_1)\theta_A$ and $\theta_A s_A=1$. Here $f_1$ denotes the appropriate endpoint-fiber map in each occurrence. Thus composition is natural up to a simplicial homotopy, with no compatibility required of the chosen sections.

source.place: Sections 5.3 and 11.2; elementary precomposition of the long-edge homotopy stated by the cited composition lemma.

proof.text:
Let $a,b$ be arbitrary objects of $\widehat U$. Essential surjectivity of $i_U$ in [lem-coef-rezk-explicit-completion] supplies $x,y$ and isomorphism representatives $\alpha:i_Ux\to a$, $\beta:i_Uy\to b$. Choose a representative $\bar\alpha:a\to i_Ux$ of the inverse class. Using the operations of [lem-coef-segal-composition-equivalences], define
$$T_U(k)=\beta\circ(k\circ\bar\alpha):M_{\widehat U}(i_Ux,i_Uy)\longrightarrow M_{\widehat U}(a,b).$$
This is the composite of precomposition by $\bar\alpha$ and postcomposition by $\beta$, hence a weak equivalence by that node and two-out-of-three from [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Define $T_V$ using $H\bar\alpha,H\beta$; these also represent isomorphisms because their inverse triangles are carried by $H$ to inverse triangles. The same cited lemma makes $T_V$ a weak equivalence. Applying step 3 twice compares $H_1T_U$ with $T_VH_1$ by a finite chain of simplicial homotopies. They realize to homotopies by [lem-coef-simplicial-realization-cylinder], and [lem-coef-homotopy-groups-basepoint-change] makes weak-equivalence status invariant under these homotopies. The left vertical map is a weak equivalence by step 2, so two-out-of-three in this square makes the right vertical map $M_{\widehat U}(a,b)\to M_{\widehat V}(Ha,Hb)$ a weak equivalence.

source.place: Section 14, completion assertion (3); Sections 5.3-5.5 and 11.2, Proposition 11.3 and Corollary 11.5 for composition by equivalences.

proof.text: Given an object $c$ of $\widehat V$, essential surjectivity of $i_V$ from [lem-coef-rezk-explicit-completion] supplies $v\in V_0$ and $c\cong i_Vv$. Essential surjectivity of $G$ supplies $u\in U_0$ and $v\cong Gu$. Applying $i_V$ and using $i_VG=H i_U$ gives $c\cong H(i_Uu)$. Thus $H$ is essentially surjective, and step 4 proves its mapping-space equivalences at every pair. Both completions are complete Segal spaces by the completion theorem. Therefore [lem-coef-complete-segal-dk-levelwise] makes every $H_n$ a weak equivalence, and [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] makes $\operatorname{diag}H$ a weak equivalence.

source.place: Section 14, assertions (1),(3); Proposition 7.6; the bisimplicial diagonal theorem.

proof.text: We next verify the diagonal of each completion unit directly; this is not a consequence of the definition of complete-Segal weak equivalence. Fix a Segal space $W$ and an integer $m\geq0$. Let $c_m:W\to W^{E(m)}$ be induced by $E(m)\to F(0)$ and let $e_m:W^{E(m)}\to W$ be evaluation at object $0$. Then $e_mc_m=1_W$. Define a functor $I[m]\times[1]\to I[m]$ on objects by $(a,0)\mapsto0$ and $(a,1)\mapsto a$; on arrows there is exactly one possible value, so it is a functor. Its nerve, regarded as discrete in the inner direction, is a map $E(m)\times F(1)\to E(m)$. Precomposition and evaluation in the cartesian internal hom give a map $W^{E(m)}\times F(1)\to W^{E(m)}$ with endpoints $c_me_m$ and $1$. Taking diagonals gives an actual simplicial homotopy with parameter $\operatorname{diag}F(1)=\Delta^1$. By [lem-coef-simplicial-realization-cylinder] it realizes to a continuous homotopy; [lem-coef-homotopy-groups-basepoint-change] then says that $\operatorname{diag}c_m$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, with inverse up to homotopy $\operatorname{diag}e_m$. The choice of object $0$ is only used to prove this for each $m$; it is not claimed natural in $m$. The maps $c_m$ themselves are natural in $m$ because collapse to the one-object groupoid is natural.

source.place: Section 14, displayed equivalence-groupoid resolution; explicit contraction argument refining the categorical-equivalence observation in Section 13.5.

proof.text: Put $D_{m,n}=(W^{E(m)})_{n,n}$. This is a bisimplicial set: the second direction is the diagonal of the outer and inner directions of $W^{E(m)}$. The natural collapses of step 6 give a map from the constant diagram $m\mapsto\operatorname{diag}W$ to $D$. Each row map is $\operatorname{diag}c_m$, a weak equivalence by step 6. Thus [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] gives a weak equivalence from $\operatorname{diag}W$ to $\operatorname{diag}D$. In degree $n$, $D_{n,n}=(W^{E(n)})_{n,n}=\widetilde W_{n,n}$, with the same three simultaneous operators, so $\operatorname{diag}D=\operatorname{diag}\widetilde W$ and this map is the diagonal of the specified raw completion unit. The map $\widetilde W\to\widehat W$ in [lem-coef-rezk-explicit-completion] is levelwise a weak equivalence, so the bisimplicial diagonal theorem applies to it as well. Composition shows that $\operatorname{diag}i_W$ is a weak equivalence.

source.place: Section 14, definition of the raw completion and Reedy replacement, with the bisimplicial diagonal theorem applied to the three indices.

proof.text: Apply step 7 to $W=U,V$. In the commuting square of step 2, both vertical diagonals $\operatorname{diag}i_U,\operatorname{diag}i_V$ and the bottom diagonal $\operatorname{diag}\widehat G$ are weak equivalences. Two-out-of-three from [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] makes $\operatorname{diag}G$ a weak equivalence. Apply the same argument to the Reedy replacement square of step 1 to obtain the required weak equivalence $\operatorname{diag}F$.

source.place: Sections 14 and 2.4; final naturality squares and two-out-of-three.

lean.note: Mapping spaces are the canonical endpoint homotopy fibers. Essential surjectivity is rendered by two inverse equations on their components using the triangle-fiber composition graph.
